text:
On a productive round we read your complaint, and a new handler looked into it. We note, for the record, that the matter concerns the handling of a companion animal during transit, the distress this caused, and the concern that the response from our staff was not prompt or reassuring.

The review shows that the animal welfare review should have been more active, and the cabin team should have kept clearer watch over the animal's condition and enclosure. The complaint is taken as a serious service lapse, and we accept that the travel experience fell below the standard expected from Aurelia Skyways. The new handler has checked the reported sequence, confirmed the file, and referred the case for immediate claim processing in the normal escape-in-transit channel. <<FACT F120>> We also confirm that the standard payout for this incident applies through the established claims route. <<FACT F114>>

In practical terms, the record now moves to the welfare coordinator, who will verify comfort concerns and assess the handling notes already on file. The cabin report will be reviewed alongside the boarding record, the hold note, and the incident log, so that the response can be corrected without delay. Where staff judgment was too slow, that shortcoming will be addressed in retraining and in the next round of oversight. Where communication failed, the gap will be recorded and escalated, since the Companion Animal Travel Desk is expected to protect both animal welfare and traveler confidence.

Please keep any supporting notes, carrier observations, and veterinary remarks ready for the claim file, as they may be requested during the review. If further contact is required, it will be made through the ordinary service record rather than by informal reply, so that the case remains complete and traceable. We regret the upset this caused and are moving the matter forward with urgency. The Companion Animal Travel Desk is continuing its review now and will keep the record in order.

Companion Animal Travel Desk
